slides.title: 5 mistakes that send guys back to p*rn [[in the last 10 days of No Nut November.]]
slides.sub: Day 20. The finish line makes people careless.

slides.title: Mistakes [[1–2]]
items: Counting down to Dec 1 like p*rn is waiting for you.
Dropping the routines that got you to Day 20.

slides.title: Mistakes [[3–4]]
items: Testing yourself — "just looking" to prove you're fine.
Staying up late because "you've earned it."

slides.title: Treating Day 30 as [[the end]]
slides.body: If November 30 is the finish line, December 1 is a p*rn binge waiting to happen. Pick a goal past the month now.

slides.title: Finish [[strong]]
items: Write your December goal on paper today.
Keep your bedtime the same until the 30th.
No tests. Avoid the content, don't prove anything.
Message one person every night until Dec 1.

carousels.name: 6 reasons secrecy keeps p*rn addiction alive (half say no one knows)

slides.title: 6 reasons secrecy keeps p*rn addiction alive — [[and half of users say no one knows.]]
slides.sub: From a survey of 2,976 U.S. adults.

slides.title: Say [[no one]] knows
slides.body: In a Barna / Pure Desire survey (2,976 U.S. adults, 2023), half of p*rn users said "no one" knows about their use. And 84% said no one helps them avoid it.

slides.title: Reasons [[1–3]]
items: No one asks, so p*rn never has to answer for itself.
Shame grows in the dark — and shame sends you back.
Every slip stays invisible, so nothing changes.

slides.title: Reasons [[4–6]]
items: You carry it alone on the worst nights.
Lying gets easier each time you hide p*rn.
Nobody can help with a problem they can't see.

slides.title: Break the [[silence]]
items: Pick one safe person — friend, brother, counselor.
Say one sentence: "I've been struggling with p*rn."
No full confession needed — just the truth.
Ask them to check in once a week.

slides.title: 6 things p*rn taught you about sex [[that aren't true.]]
slides.sub: Most of it was never meant to be real.

slides.title: Lies [[1–2]]
items: "Everyone is always ready." Real people need time, mood and trust.
"It's a performance." Real intimacy isn't a show for a camera.

slides.title: Lies [[3–4]]
items: "Bodies look like that." P*rn is cast, lit and edited.
"Asking kills the mood." Asking is how trust gets built.

slides.title: Lies [[5–6]]

carousels.name: 3 reasons you'll go back to p*rn with 10 days of NNN left

slides.title: 3 reasons you'll go back to p*rn [[with 10 days of No Nut November left.]]
slides.sub: Read them now, so they don't happen.

slides.title: You think you've [[won]]
slides.body: Twenty days in, you feel fine. So you relax. P*rn doesn't need you weak. It needs you careless.

slides.title: You never had a [[why]]
slides.body: "Everyone was doing it" got you started. It won't get you through Day 27. A challenge isn't a reason to quit p*rn.

slides.title: You're [[bargaining]]
slides.body: "It's basically a month anyway." "Just once won't matter." That's not logic. That's the craving talking.

slides.title: Don't let it [[happen]]
items: Write your real reason in one sentence. Read it every night.
Say the bargain out loud — it sounds weaker that way.
Remove the last loophole you've been saving.
Plan Nov 30 night now, hour by hour.

carousels.name: 7 habits of people who actually quit p*rn for good

slides.title: 7 habits of people who actually [[quit p*rn for good.]]
slides.sub: What many long-term quitters say they do.

slides.title: Habits [[1–3]]
items: They plan evenings — when p*rn usually wins.
They tell someone, and keep telling them.
They avoid the gray zone, not only p*rn itself.

slides.title: Habits [[4–5]]
items: They treat slips as data, not as proof they're broken.
They move every day — even a 15-minute walk.

slides.title: Habits [[6–7]]
items: They sleep on schedule — tired brains bargain.
They build a life they don't need to escape from.

slides.title: Start with [[one]]
slides.body: Nobody does all seven on day one. Pick the habit you're weakest at and practice it this week. That's how p*rn loses ground.
